title: By the mount where Allah spoke to Musa.
subtitle: Why a mountain opens the surah
then: The tafsir says Allah swears by His creation {idea}as a testimony to His great ability.{/idea} At-Tur is a mount with trees, like the one {reward}where Allah spoke to Musa.{/reward} The Prophet ﷺ was heard reciting this surah in Maghrib, and a listener said he never heard a more beautiful recitation.
now: You have a place that changed you: the masjid where you first cried in prayer, a hospital chapel, a quiet beach at dawn. {idea}Places can testify.{/idea} This surah starts at one of the greatest of them.
old: A mountain is just part of the scenery.
new: Some places carry the memory of Allah speaking, and they call me to listen.
try: Go back, in person or in memory, to one place where you felt close to Allah, and sit there for five minutes.

title: By a Book that is already written.
subtitle: The inscribed Book
then: Allah swears by {idea}a Book inscribed.{/idea} The tafsir gives two views: the Preserved Tablet, or {idea}the revealed Books that people recite.{/idea} Either way, what is written with Allah does not change.
now: You write a to-do list and lose it by Tuesday. Contracts get rewritten, promises get broken. {idea}This Book does not get rewritten.{/idea} What Allah promises in it is as firm as ink that never fades.
old: Promises are words that can change.
new: Allah's word is written and fixed. His promise is the most certain thing there is.
try: Open the Quran today and read one page slowly, as words that will not change.

title: Written on open parchment, spread out to be read.
subtitle: A Book meant to be opened
then: The Book is {reward}in parchment unrolled.{/reward} The tafsir links this to the revealed Books {idea}that people recite.{/idea} It is not a sealed secret but something laid open.
now: There is a Quran in your house, maybe wrapped in cloth on the top shelf, opened in Ramadan and at funerals. {reward}It was sent spread open.{/reward} It is meant for your Tuesday evenings too.
old: The Quran is precious, so I keep it safely closed.
new: Its honor is in being opened and read, not only kept.
try: Take the Quran off the shelf and leave it somewhere you will see it tomorrow.

title: By the House in heaven always full of worshippers.
subtitle: Al-Bayt Al-Ma'mur
then: The Prophet ﷺ said that on the Night Journey he was taken to {idea}Al-Bayt Al-Ma'mur{/idea}, visited daily by seventy thousand angels who never return to it again. He saw Ibrahim reclining against it. The tafsir notes {reward}Ibrahim built the Ka'bah on earth, and the reward fits the action.{/reward}
now: You feel like you are praying alone in a small room. Right now, angels without number are circling a House in heaven. {idea}Your prayer joins a worship that never stops.{/idea}
old: My worship is small and lonely.
new: My prayer joins a worship in heaven that never pauses.
try: In your next prayer, remember for a moment that the angels are worshipping with you.

title: By the roof raised high above you.
subtitle: The sky as a guarded ceiling
then: Ali bin Abi Talib said the raised roof {idea}means the heaven{/idea}, and recited: We made the heaven a roof, {reward}safe and well-guarded{/reward}, {trap}yet they turn away from its signs.{/trap}
now: You notice the ceiling only when it leaks. The sky over your city has never leaked, never cracked, never fallen. {idea}A guarded roof you never pay for.{/idea} Most days you never even look at it.
old: I only notice the roof over me when something goes wrong.
new: The sky is a roof Allah keeps guarded for me every second.
try: Look up at the sky once today and thank Allah for the roof you never had to fix.

title: By the sea that is full, and will one day blaze.
subtitle: The calm sea and what it will become

row.title: the sea will always be calm

then: Most scholars say this is {idea}the oceans of the earth.{/idea} One view in the tafsir: on the Day of Resurrection {trap}the sea will be kindled with fire{/trap}, as in another verse. Qatadah and Ibn Jarir preferred {idea}the filled sea{/idea}, since it is not lit now.
now: You stand on a beach, the waves steady, the horizon endless. It feels like it will always be this way. {idea}Nothing in creation is fixed except by Allah's will.{/idea} The world you think is permanent has a last day.
old: The world around me is solid and will stay the same.
new: Even the oceans are held in place by Allah, and one day they will change.
try: Next time you see water, a sea, a river, or a glass, remember for a moment that it obeys Allah.

title: Everything sworn by points to this: it will happen.
subtitle: The answer to the oaths

row.title: a true vow
sub: it stopped him in the street

then: After five oaths comes the point: {trap}the punishment of your Lord will surely come to pass.{/trap} The tafsir reports that Umar once heard a man reciting this at night in Madinah and said, {idea}by the Lord of the Ka'bah, this is a true vow.{/idea} He went home and was ill for a month.
now: You have heard this verse in Taraweeh, maybe a dozen times, and it slid past. Umar heard it once through a wall and sat down in the street. {idea}Let one verse actually land on you.{/idea}
old: I know these verses already. They are familiar.
new: Familiar words can still be true vows that should stop me.
try: Read this one verse slowly three times today, and sit with it for a minute.

title: When it comes, nothing can push it back.
subtitle: No preventer
then: The tafsir says that {trap}when Allah decides to send the torment, none can prevent it or stop it.{/trap} The Makkans had wealth, tribes, and alliances. None of that would be a shield. {idea}This is the part of the vow that shook Umar.{/idea}
now: You have a lawyer for a contract, insurance for the car, a friend who knows someone. You can push almost anything back a little. {idea}This one, no one can.{/idea} {reward}But today the door to turn back is wide open.{/reward}
old: There is always someone who can get me out of trouble.
new: Some things no one can stop, so the time to prepare is now.
try: Make sincere istighfar for something specific, while the door is still open.

title: The sky that held still will shake and spin.
subtitle: The raised roof, on that Day
then: Verse 5 swore by the roof raised high. Now that same sky {trap}will sway with circular motion.{/trap} The tafsir gives the meanings: shaking violently, splitting, spinning. {idea}The word holds both shaking and spinning.{/idea}
now: An earthquake alert buzzes on your phone and for three seconds everything you trusted feels unsteady. {idea}That feeling is a tiny preview.{/idea} The only firm ground is what you built with Allah.
old: The world under and above me is stable.
new: Only Allah is truly stable. Even the sky will move when He commands.
try: Say one dua today asking Allah to make you steady on the Day when everything shakes.

title: The mountains will move off like dust.
subtitle: What seems fixed forever
then: The surah opened with a mountain. Now {trap}the mountains will pass on, departing.{/trap} The tafsir says they will fade away and become {trap}scattered particles of dust blown away by the wind.{/trap}
now: You say solid as a rock about your job, your health, your plans. The rocks themselves will blow away like dust. {idea}Anchor yourself to what does not move.{/idea}
old: Some things in my life are rock solid.
new: Even mountains will become dust. Only what is with Allah stays.
try: Name one thing you call permanent. Then do one small deed that will truly last.

title: That Day will be heavy for those who denied it.
subtitle: Woe to the deniers

row.title: the deniers
sub: who said it would not come

then: With the sky shaking and mountains gone, the verse turns to people: {trap}woe that Day to those who denied.{/trap} The tafsir says the woe is the punishment Allah directs at them. The surah introduction notes that the Makkans called the Prophet ﷺ a sorcerer and a madman.
now: You do not deny the Day out loud. But some weeks you live as if it is not coming: no prayer, no thought of it. {idea}Denial can be quiet.{/idea} It shows in how you spend your days.
old: I believe in the Day, so this does not apply to me.
new: Belief shows in how I live, not only in what I say.
try: Look at yesterday honestly. Find one moment where you lived as if the Day was not real, and change it today.

title: They spent their days in empty talk and play.
subtitle: Who the deniers were
then: The deniers are described: {trap}those who were, in their falsehood, playing.{/trap} The tafsir says they live in falsehood and {trap}make the religion the subject of their mockery and jest.{/trap}
now: Hours in a group chat trading memes about religion. A comedy show where faith is always the punchline. You laugh along. {idea}Play is fine. Making the sacred a joke is not.{/idea}
old: Joking about religion is harmless.
new: What I keep laughing at slowly becomes what I cannot take seriously.
try: Next time a joke about faith comes up, simply do not add to it.

title: Those who played will be driven, not invited.
subtitle: From playing to being pushed
then: The people of verse 12 lived in jest. Now the scene flips: {trap}they will be violently driven and shoved{/trap} toward the Fire, as the tafsir explains. The ones who refused to walk toward Allah {idea}lose the choice to walk at all.{/idea}
now: Today nobody forces you to pray, read, or apologize. You can walk to it on your own feet, at your own pace. {reward}That freedom is a mercy{/reward}, and it does not last forever.
old: I have plenty of time to choose later.
new: The freedom to walk toward Allah is a gift I have now, not forever.
try: Walk to one good deed today on your own: a prayer, a visit, a charity, without waiting to be pushed.

title: This is the very thing you said was not real.
subtitle: When denial meets the fact
then: The tafsir says {trap}the angels of punishment will say these words{/trap} to them, admonishing them: {trap}this is the Fire which you used to deny.{/trap} What they mocked as a story is now in front of them.
now: You ignored the bill, and now it is a court letter. You skipped the checkups, and now it is a diagnosis. {idea}Not looking did not make it go away.{/idea} The kindest time to face something is early.
old: If I do not think about it, it is not real for me.
new: Denying something does not change it. It only leaves me unprepared.
try: Face one thing you have been avoiding: open the letter, book the appointment, or make the call.

title: Is this magic too, or can you not see?
subtitle: The old excuse, thrown back

row.title: it is magic
sub: what they said of the message

then: The Makkans called the Prophet ﷺ a sorcerer, as the surah introduction notes, so they could wave away the message. On the Day they are asked: {trap}is this magic, or do you not see?{/trap} {idea}The trick was never in the message. It was in their refusal to look.{/idea}
now: You have a favorite excuse that makes any uncomfortable truth go away: it is just propaganda, they are just exaggerating. {idea}Ask whether the excuse is protecting you or blinding you.{/idea}
old: I can explain away anything I do not want to accept.
new: An excuse that dismisses every truth is a blindfold, not a shield.
try: Notice the excuse you reach for most often today. Ask once: what if the other side is right?

title: You are only repaid for what you did.
subtitle: Justice, not cruelty
then: The tafsir says whether they endure it or not, {trap}they will never avert it.{/trap} Then the key line: {idea}you are only requited for what you used to do{/idea}, and {reward}Allah is never unjust with anyone.{/reward}
now: Today your patience still matters: with your kids, your illness, your hard boss. It earns reward and changes outcomes. {reward}This is the life where patience works.{/reward} Spend it here.
old: What happens to me in the end is out of my hands.
new: Allah repays deeds with justice, and today my deeds and patience still count.
try: Choose one hard moment today and meet it with patience, for Allah's sake.

title: The mindful will be in gardens and delight.
subtitle: The other side of the Day
then: Right after the scene of the deniers, the tafsir says Allah {idea}described the destination of the happy ones{/idea}, in contrast: {reward}those who have taqwa will be in gardens and delight.{/reward}
now: You make many small choices nobody sees: lowering your eyes, holding your tongue in a fight, giving when it is tight. {reward}Each one is a step toward a garden.{/reward}
old: Being careful about Allah just makes life heavier.
new: Mindfulness of Allah is the road to delight, not away from it.
try: Make one quiet choice today purely because Allah is watching.

title: Enjoying His gifts, and saved from the Fire.
subtitle: Two blessings at once
then: The tafsir lists {reward}foods, drinks, clothes, dwelling places, mounts{/reward}. Then it says being saved from the Fire {idea}is a bounty itself.{/idea} On top of that, Paradise has delights {reward}no eye has seen, no ear has heard.{/reward}
now: You thank Allah for the new job. You rarely thank Him for the car crash that did not happen, the illness you never got, the argument that never blew up. {idea}Being spared is a gift too.{/idea}
old: I only count the good things I get.
new: What Allah protects me from is as much a gift as what He gives.
try: Thank Allah tonight for one harm you were spared this week.

title: Eat and drink happily, for what you used to do.
subtitle: The welcome they hear
then: Verse 16 said the deniers are repaid for what they used to do. Here the same idea comes back as a welcome: {reward}eat and drink with happiness because of what you used to do.{/reward} The tafsir adds that {idea}all this is a favor from Allah and a reward from Him.{/idea}
now: The fasts in summer heat. The nights you dragged yourself up for Fajr. The meals you shared when your own fridge was half empty. {reward}None of it is forgotten.{/reward}
old: My small good deeds disappear and do not matter.
new: Every deed I send ahead is waiting for me, turned into joy.
try: Feed someone today, even a snack or a coffee, and remember this verse.

title: Reclining face to face, with spouses given by Allah.
subtitle: Rest, company, and companionship
then: They will {reward}recline with ease on thrones{/reward}, which the tafsir explains as {idea}facing each other{/idea}, as in another verse. Allah adds that He will give them {reward}righteous spouses{/reward} of great beauty.
now: Think of the best evening you have had: tired, fed, sitting with people you love, nobody looking at a phone. {reward}Paradise is described like that, but without an end.{/reward} The people you sit with now matter.
old: Rest is something I steal between tasks.
new: True rest, with good company, is part of what Allah promises.
try: Tonight, put the phones away and sit face to face with someone you love for ten minutes.

title: Believing children will be raised to join their parents.
subtitle: Families reunited, and each soul accountable
then: Ibn Abbas said Allah {reward}elevates the believers' offspring to the rank of their parents{/reward} so the parents' eyes are comforted. The tafsir also cites the hadith that a righteous child's prayer raises a parent. Then: {idea}every person is a pledge for what he earned.{/idea}
now: You worry about your kids at university, about whether your faith will pass on. {reward}Allah promises to gather believing families.{/reward} And your own dua for your late parent still reaches them.
old: My family's faith is scattered and out of my hands.
new: Allah reunites believing families and lets love carry across, while judging each fairly.
try: Make dua today for your parents by name, living or passed.

title: Fruit and meat, whatever they wish for.
subtitle: Provision that never runs out
then: The tafsir explains: {reward}various types and kinds of fruits and meat{/reward}, {idea}whatever they wish for and desire.{/idea} After the promise of family reunited, comes the promise of provision without limit.
now: You scroll through food delivery apps, wanting something but not sure what, and nothing quite satisfies. {idea}Desire here is never fully met.{/idea} {reward}There, it will be.{/reward}
old: If I just get the next thing I want, I will be satisfied.
new: Full satisfaction is promised in Paradise, so I can be gentle with my wants here.
try: At your next meal, eat slowly and say Alhamdulillah for each part of it.

title: A shared cup, with no foul talk and no sin.
subtitle: Gathering without regret
then: The tafsir says that when they drink, {reward}they do not say any idle, vain words or sinful speech{/reward} like drunken people in this life. Qatadah said Allah {idea}purified the drink of the Hereafter from the ills and harm{/idea} of this life's drink.
now: You leave a party or a late night out and the next morning you regret what you said. The jokes went too far. {idea}Picture a gathering you never regret.{/idea}
old: Having a good time means letting myself say anything.
new: The best gatherings leave no regret behind.
try: At your next gathering, steer one conversation away from gossip.

title: Served by youths as fine as hidden pearls.
subtitle: Honored, not serving
then: The tafsir says these are the servants the believers will have in Paradise: {reward}beautiful, graceful, clean and neat as well-preserved pearls.{/reward} {idea}They go round to serve them.{/idea}
now: You serve all day: the customers, the patients, the kids, the elderly parent. Nobody brings you anything. {reward}Allah sees every plate you carry for others{/reward}, and honors you in return.
old: My service to others goes unnoticed.
new: Allah notices every act of service and returns it with honor.
try: Serve someone today with intention for Allah, then thank Him for letting you.

title: In Paradise, friends turn to each other and talk.
subtitle: Remembering the road together

row.title: the journey that got them there

then: The tafsir says {reward}the believers will draw near to each other talking{/reward} and {idea}remembering their actions and conditions in this life{/idea}, the way friends talk over a meal.
now: Picture yourself one day with the friend who prayed beside you in a cold masjid, laughing about how hard it was. {reward}The people you strive with now are your future conversation.{/reward}
old: My struggles now are just something to get through.
new: The struggles I share with good friends become stories we tell in Paradise.
try: Send a message to a friend who helps you in your faith and tell them you are grateful for them.

title: We were careful with Allah, even at home.
subtitle: Fear in the middle of family life
then: Their first memory: {idea}in the midst of our families{/idea}, the tafsir says, {idea}we were afraid of our Lord and fearful of His torment.{/idea} Their awareness of Allah was not saved for special places. It lived at home.
now: Home is where you relax. It is also where you snap at your spouse, ignore your mother's call, scroll past Isha. {idea}Mindfulness at the dinner table counts.{/idea}
old: Home is where I can be careless.
new: The way I live with my family is part of my walk with Allah.
try: At home today, catch one harsh word before it comes out and say something kind instead.

title: Allah was gracious and saved us from what we feared.
subtitle: Fear that ended in safety
then: They say: {reward}Allah has been gracious to us{/reward}, and {reward}saved us from the torment of the Fire.{/reward} The tafsir says, {idea}He granted us a favor and saved us from what we feared.{/idea} They do not credit themselves.
now: You sat by the hospital bed fearing the worst, and it passed. You panicked about the bills, and somehow they were paid. {reward}Remember who saved you.{/reward} Fear placed with Allah ends in safety.
old: I got through hard times because of my own strength.
new: When I am saved from what I feared, it is Allah's favor.
try: Recall one fear that did not come true. Thank Allah for it out loud.

title: We used to call on Him, and He is Kind and Merciful.
subtitle: The dua that was answered
then: Their last words in this scene: {idea}we used to invoke Him before.{/idea} The tafsir says they called on Him {idea}with submission and humility{/idea}, and {reward}He accepted and gave them what they wished.{/reward}
now: The dua you whisper in the car before the job interview. The one you make in sujood when no one knows what you are carrying. {reward}Those duas are not lost.{/reward} One day you may say: I used to call on Him.
old: My duas feel small and maybe unheard.
new: The duas I make now are part of how I reach Paradise.
try: Make one dua today in your own words, in sujood, for something you truly want.

title: Keep reminding. You are no fortune-teller and no madman.
subtitle: Allah defends His Prophet ﷺ

key.label: What to do with false labels

then: The surah turns to the Quraysh chiefs. Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ to {idea}keep conveying the message{/idea}, and answers their claims: {reward}by the grace of Allah, you are neither a soothsayer nor a madman.{/reward}
now: Someone spreads a story about you at work or in the family. You want to spend a week correcting it. {idea}Keep doing the good you were doing.{/idea} Let Allah handle your name.
old: I have to clear my name before I can carry on.
new: When I am lied about, I keep doing right and trust Allah to defend me.
try: If someone has misjudged you, do one good thing today without explaining yourself.

title: They called him a poet and waited for him to die.
subtitle: Waiting for a messenger to disappear
then: Ibn Abbas reported that the Quraysh met in Dar An-Nadwah, and one said: {trap}jail him in chains, then wait{/trap}; he will die like the poets before him. They hoped time would {trap}rid them of his message.{/trap}
now: You have a reminder you are waiting out: a nagging conscience, a friend's advice, a verse that bothers you. {idea}You hope it will fade if you ignore it long enough.{/idea} Truth does not expire.
old: If I ignore an uncomfortable truth long enough, it will go away.
new: Truth does not fade with time. Waiting it out only delays my answer.
try: Bring one ignored piece of good advice back to mind today and act on part of it.

title: Then wait. I am waiting with you.
subtitle: A calm answer to people waiting for your fall
then: Allah gives the Prophet ﷺ a short, calm reply: {idea}wait, and I too will wait with you.{/idea} The tafsir adds, {reward}you will come to know to whom the good end and triumph shall be granted{/reward}, in this life and the next.
now: A rival at work is waiting for you to fail. A relative says your new path will not last. {idea}You do not need to argue.{/idea} Keep going and let time tell.
old: I have to prove them wrong right now.
new: I can calmly wait, trusting Allah to show whose path ends well.
try: When someone doubts you this week, smile, say we will see, and keep going.

title: Does your mind really tell you this, or is it pride?
subtitle: Reason or rebellion
then: The Quraysh prided themselves on being sensible. Allah asks: {idea}do their minds command them to say this{/idea}, though the tafsir says {trap}they know in their hearts it is untrue?{/trap} Or are they simply {trap}a people who transgress all bounds?{/trap}
now: You give a long logical reason for skipping something you know is right. But underneath, you just do not want to. {idea}Be honest about which one is speaking: your reason, or your resistance.{/idea}
old: My objections are purely logical.
new: Sometimes my reasons are really my resistance, dressed as logic.
try: Take one excuse you use often. Ask yourself honestly: is this reason, or reluctance?

title: They said he made it up. Really, they refused to believe.
subtitle: The accusation and its root
then: They said the Prophet ﷺ {trap}forged this Quran and brought it from his own.{/trap} Allah answers with one line: {idea}rather, they do not believe.{/idea} The tafsir says {trap}their disbelief drives them to utter these statements.{/trap}
now: When you have decided you do not like someone, every rumor about them sounds believable. {idea}The verdict came first, the reasons second.{/idea} Watch for that in yourself.
old: I doubt things because the evidence is weak.
new: Sometimes I decide first and gather reasons after.
try: Think of one person you are quick to suspect. Give them one fair benefit of the doubt today.

title: If it was made up, bring something like it.
subtitle: The challenge of the Quran
then: If he wrote it himself, Allah says, {idea}let them produce a recitation like it.{/idea} The tafsir says that even if they joined with all jinn and mankind, {reward}they would never produce something like the Quran, or ten surahs, or even one.{/reward}
now: You have read thousands of posts, articles, and books this year. How many of them changed how you pray, forgive, or sleep at night? {reward}This book has been doing that for fourteen centuries.{/reward}
old: The Quran is one great book among many.
new: The Quran stands alone, and no one has matched it.
try: Read a short surah today, slowly, and notice one line that speaks to you.

title: Did you come from nothing, or did you make yourself?
subtitle: The question that opened a heart
then: Jubayr bin Mut'im came to the Prophet ﷺ after Badr, still an idolator. He heard him recite these verses in Maghrib and said, {reward}I felt my heart would fly away.{/reward} The tafsir says this was {idea}one of the reasons he later embraced Islam.{/idea}
now: You call yourself self-made: your degree, your business, your body at the gym. But you did not make your heart beat this morning. {idea}Ask the question honestly, once.{/idea}
old: I am who I am because of my own effort.
new: I did not create myself. Someone made me, and that changes everything.
try: Put your hand on your chest, feel your heartbeat for thirty seconds, and ask who keeps it going.

title: They did not make the sky. They just lack certainty.
subtitle: Knowing, but not being sure
then: The tafsir says {idea}they knew that Allah alone is the Creator{/idea}. Yet they fell into idolatry because {trap}they had no firm belief.{/trap} Knowledge without certainty did not change how they lived.
now: You know Allah provides, but you still lose sleep over money. You know He hears, but you still do not ask. {idea}The gap between knowing and being certain is where most of us live.{/idea}
old: Knowing something about Allah is the same as being sure of it.
new: Certainty is knowledge that has reached the heart and shows in my life.
try: Pick one thing you know about Allah, and act today as if you are fully certain of it.

title: Do they hold the keys to your Lord's treasures?
subtitle: Who is actually in charge
then: The Quraysh chiefs acted as if they decided who deserved a prophet. Allah asks: {trap}do they hold the keys to His treasures?{/trap} The tafsir answers, {reward}never; Allah is the only King and Owner of existence{/reward}, and He does what He wills.
now: You watch someone else get the job, the baby, the blessing, and you quietly feel it should have been decided differently. {idea}The treasures are His, not yours or theirs.{/idea}
old: I know better who deserves what.
new: Allah holds the treasures, and He gives as He wills, wisely.
try: Next time you feel envy, say MashaAllah for the other person and ask Allah for good for yourself.

title: Do they have a ladder to heaven to hear its news?
subtitle: Show the proof
then: Do they have {trap}a stairway to heaven{/trap}, where the angels are, to hear things? Then {idea}let their listener produce manifest proof.{/idea} The tafsir says {trap}they will never be able to do so.{/trap}
now: Someone in the family chat is sure about what will happen, what Allah wants, who is going to Hell. They speak like they heard it directly. {idea}Ask: what is your proof?{/idea} Ask yourself the same.
old: If I feel sure about something in religion, I must be right.
new: Claims about the unseen need proof from Allah, not just confidence.
try: Before repeating a religious claim today, check its source first.

title: They gave Allah daughters while wanting sons for themselves.
subtitle: A double standard exposed

row.title: sons for ourselves
sub: faces dark at a girl's birth

then: The pagans preferred sons, and when told of a daughter, {trap}a man's face would turn dark with suppressed anger{/trap}, says the tafsir. Yet {trap}they made the angels Allah's daughters{/trap} and worshipped them. The verse exposes the contradiction.
now: You hold others to rules you never apply to yourself. The colleague is lazy, but you are tired. Your cousin is stingy, but you are careful. {idea}A double standard tells on the heart.{/idea}
old: My standards are fair.
new: When I judge others by one rule and myself by another, something is wrong in me.
try: Catch one double standard in yourself today and apply your rule to yourself instead.

title: He asks no payment. Why act as if he sends a bill?
subtitle: Free guidance, treated like a debt
then: The surah introduction says they {trap}avoided him as if he was asking them for a reward.{/trap} Allah asks: do you ask them a wage, {trap}so they are weighed down with debt?{/trap} The tafsir says no, he asked for nothing.
now: A friend gives you honest advice for free, and you react like they handed you an invoice. {reward}Good counsel that costs you nothing is a gift.{/reward}
old: Advice from others is a burden on me.
new: Honest guidance given freely is a gift, not a debt.
try: Thank the last person who gave you honest advice, even if it stung.

title: Do they know the unseen, writing it down?
subtitle: Only Allah knows what is hidden
then: Do they have the unseen, {trap}so they write it down?{/trap} The tafsir says they do not, for {idea}none in the heavens or earth knows the unseen except Allah.{/idea} Their confidence about the Hereafter had no basis.
now: You are sure you will have time to repent later, sure your plans for ten years will work out, sure you know how someone's story ends. {idea}None of that is written in your hand.{/idea}
old: I know how things will turn out.
new: The future is with Allah, so I act well today.
try: Replace one I will later with something you do today.

title: Their plot turns back on the plotters.
subtitle: Schemes against the truth
then: The surah introduction says the chiefs {trap}took counsel together to devise schemes{/trap} against the Prophet ﷺ. Allah says the disbelievers are the ones plotted against. The tafsir explains: {idea}their plots will only harm them.{/idea}
now: You plan how to get back at the coworker who embarrassed you: the cc on the email, the comment in the meeting. {idea}Schemes have a way of coming home.{/idea} Let it go, and let Allah handle it.
old: If I plan carefully, I can get back at them.
new: Scheming harms the schemer most. I can leave the account with Allah.
try: Drop one small plan to get even with someone today.

title: Is there any god but Allah? Glory to Him above it.
subtitle: The last question in the chain
then: After a long string of or do they questions, the last one: {trap}or have they a god other than Allah?{/trap} The tafsir calls it {idea}a harsh refutation{/idea} of calling on rivals with Him, then Allah {reward}glorifies Himself above their idolatry.{/reward}
now: You may not have idols, but you have things you cannot say no to: approval, the scale, the salary figure. {idea}Ask which of them you obey like a god.{/idea} Then say SubhanAllah and mean it.
old: Idolatry is something from the past.
new: Anything I obey over Allah is a rival. He is above them all.
try: Say SubhanAllah 33 times after one prayer today, thinking of what it means.

title: Even a falling sky, they would call just clouds.
subtitle: When no sign is ever enough
then: The tafsir says that if punishment came at them from the sky, {trap}they would not believe it was coming their way{/trap}. They would call it layers of clouds. It cites another verse: given a gate to heaven, {trap}they would say our eyes are dazzled.{/trap}
now: The third warning from your doctor. The friend who drifts away after the same argument. You call it bad timing each time. {idea}At some point, the clouds are not clouds.{/idea}
old: Each warning I get is just a coincidence.
new: A heart that explains away every sign will never see one.
try: Take one repeated warning in your life seriously today, and write down what it might be telling you.

title: Leave them until they meet their Day.
subtitle: Not every argument is yours to win
then: After the clouds verse, Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ: {idea}leave them alone{/idea} until they meet their Day. The tafsir says this is {trap}the Day of Resurrection{/trap}, when they will faint in terror.
now: You have argued with the same person about faith for years. Every holiday dinner, round two. {idea}You can stop.{/idea} Live well, make dua, and leave the final word to Allah.
old: If I stop arguing, I am giving up on them.
new: Sometimes stepping back and leaving it to Allah is the right step.
try: Skip one argument you know will go nowhere, and make dua for that person instead.

title: That Day, all their scheming will be worth nothing.
subtitle: Plans that will not help
then: The chiefs had held council after council. The tafsir says {trap}their deceit and plots{/trap} shall not help them in the least on that Day, {trap}nor will they be helped.{/trap}
now: You are good at angles: the clever excuse, the right contact, the loophole. It works at work and with the tax forms. {idea}None of it works on that Day.{/idea} {reward}Only honest deeds do.{/reward}
old: With the right strategy, I can get out of anything.
new: On the Day, no strategy helps. Only what I did sincerely.
try: Choose the straight way today in one place where you usually take a clever shortcut.

title: Smaller trials come first, so people might return.
subtitle: Hardship as a wake-up call
then: The tafsir says Allah tests them with {trap}various hardships in this world{/trap} so {reward}they might go back and repent{/reward}, citing a verse about the near torment. But most {trap}revert to the worst of what they did{/trap} once it is lifted.
now: The scare, the layoff, the night in the ER. You promised Allah you would change. Then it passed and so did the promise. {idea}The hard days were the invitation.{/idea}
old: Hard times are just bad luck to get through.
new: Hardships can be Allah calling me back before it is too late.
try: Remember one promise you made to Allah in a hard time. Keep a piece of it today.

title: Be patient. You are under Our eyes.
subtitle: Seen and protected
then: After all their insults, Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ: {idea}be patient{/idea}, for {reward}you are under Our eyes and protection.{/reward} Then: glorify Him when you rise. The tafsir mentions rising for prayer, from sleep, and the hadith of saying SubhanakAllahumma wa bihamdik before leaving a gathering.
now: The meeting where you were talked over. The scroll of comments under your post. You feel unseen and alone. {reward}You are seen.{/reward} Patience is lighter when you know Who is watching.
old: No one sees what I put up with.
new: Allah sees me and protects me, so I can be patient.
try: Before leaving your next gathering, say SubhanakAllahumma wa bihamdik.

title: Praise Him at night, and as the stars fade.
subtitle: The surah ends at dawn

key.label: What those two rak'ahs are worth

then: The tafsir says the night glorification means {idea}reciting the Quran and praying at night.{/idea} The setting of the stars refers to the two sunnah rak'ahs before Fajr. Aishah said the Prophet ﷺ was never more regular in any voluntary prayer, and he said {reward}they are better than this world and all in it.{/reward}
now: The alarm goes off before Fajr and the bed is warm. Two extra rak'ahs take three minutes. {reward}Better than everything in your bank account, your feed, your plans.{/reward} The stars are fading anyway.
old: The extra prayers before Fajr are too small to matter.
new: Two quiet rak'ahs as the stars fade are worth more than the whole world.
try: Tomorrow, pray the two rak'ahs before Fajr, even if quickly.
